name: batch-09
prompt:
Create ONE production game-icon SPRITE ATLAS, exactly 3 columns by 3 rows on a square canvas, ideally 2048x2048, genuinely TRANSPARENT alpha PNG. Input image is the user's approved style sheet, STYLE reference only. Match that soft tactile dimensional 3D collectible family: gentle warm upper-left diffuse studio light, rounded yet faithful forms, bright pastel/candy color, subtle ambient occlusion, restrained material detail. Each object's true material remains recognizable: paper, wood, glass, metal, woven cloth. No same-clay treatment on everything. No heavy dark outlines or flat vector art.

CRITICAL PACKAGING: There are EXACTLY NINE equal square virtual cells in a regular 3x3 grid. Draw ONE specified object/group centered within EACH virtual cell, at ONLY 48–52% of cell width/height, with at least 24% EMPTY TRANSPARENT MARGIN ON EVERY SIDE. Nothing may touch a virtual cell edge or cross into a neighbor. All strings, handles, leaves and shadows stay inside their own cell. Think SMALL MINIATURE ICONS with LARGE EMPTY GUTTERS, NOT large illustrations filling the sheet. Icon centers are x=16.67%,50%,83.33%, y=16.67%,50%,83.33% of the image. Each icon must fit in a box 18% of the overall image size. Empty space between shapes is essential. No visible grid lines, no backgrounds, no color squares, no borders, no captions, numbers, words, ID labels, titles or decorative props. Empty padding is genuine alpha transparency, NOT a drawn checkerboard. Top-left through bottom-right order is mandatory; do not swap cells. Each tile will be cropped at exact one-third boundaries into a separate icon. Keep centered and similarly weighted, readable at 32–66px. All objects fully in frame, no cropping. Only allow inscription glyphs explicitly specified in subject. Do not invent sacred symbols, cultural ornament, claims or text. No extra humans/hands/landscape/pedestals. Subject list in strict row-major order:
1. Cell row 1, column 1: A compact sage-and-straw woven four-armed cross, with a tightly interlaced square center, four bent rectangular rush bundles and pale bindings near the ends; preserve the woven pinwheel construction rather than a plain solid cross.
2. Cell row 1, column 2: A pale golden bamboo rice scoop-strainer with a broad shallow woven basket, short upright loop handle, a few ivory rice grains and two small dusty-coral cord ends below; preserve the curved open basket and visible weave.
3. Cell row 1, column 3: A pale honey-colored pentagonal wooden plaque with a shallow roof-shaped top, two dark upper holes and one tan hanging cord; a small original pink flower and sage stem decorate its face, without readable script or a copied crest.
4. Cell row 2, column 1: A pale mint cotton strip tied over a low tan tree branch, with soft vertical folds; beside it sits a short gray stone well ring containing blue-green water, with no healing symbols or added offerings.
5. Cell row 2, column 2: One shallow terracotta oil lamp with an asymmetric pointed lip, a warm golden oil surface, curved ivory cotton wick and a small yellow flame at the raised right edge; preserve the open clay bowl shape.
6. Cell row 2, column 3: One upright cream wax candle with small wax drips, a dark wick and warm golden flame, standing on a simple muted stone-colored candle stand with short gray metal side rails; no printed image or added religious emblem.
7. Cell row 3, column 1: A tall cream folded paper gift envelope wrapped horizontally with coral and gold paper cords, forming an original symmetrical multi-loop knot with two short diagonal tails; keep the cords slender and distinct, without invented writing or a specified ceremonial knot.
8. Cell row 3, column 2: A small warm-gold metal heart token pinned by a round gold tack to the cream inset of a tan rectangular wooden display board; retain the simple rounded heart shape, without adding flames, wings or lettering.
9. Cell row 3, column 3: A small circular garland of ivory flower buds with a few soft-pink accents, an open center and two short cream trailing strands ending in pink flower clusters; preserve the compact ring and paired pendants.
